long_biography.plain_text:
Born in 1862, Arthur Kendall Stothert entered engineering and worked in Glasgow’s port industry, where cranes and other heavy equipment formed the commercial setting of his career. By the early twentieth century he was living in Kensington, London, while retaining the professional and sporting associations that connected him to the Clyde.

Stothert was also one of the era’s most committed competitive sailors and racing patrons. Beginning in the 1890s, he built a long competitive record and worked repeatedly with Scottish designer William Fife III. His campaigns were marked by intensive participation, technical scrutiny and strong results, placing him among the prominent British sailors of the years before the First World War. He died in 1929.

Kendall is therefore proposed as the missing middle name and the display name is normalised without altering the immutable source snapshot.

The Guggenheim Bilbao exhibition catalogue supplies the 1862-1929 life span for the exact Glasgow engineer and yachtsman. It does not provide day or month, and no equally strong reviewed record filled them. The marriage record names his father as John Lum Stothert of Audley, Bath, and a local-history source records Arthur and Percy Kendall Stothert as joint freeholders. These links explain the family context but do not document a capital transfer or inheritance. No family wealth is attributed to Arthur beyond what exact-person sources support.
